appraisal_events.evidence: Je nage dans la joie, parce que vous avez fait la conquête de mon grand ami Bergotte. Il a dit à maman qu'il vous avait trouvé extrêmement intelligent.
appraisal_events.explanation: After a passage of anxious self-doubt in which the narrator was convinced he had seemed stupid to Bergotte, Gilberte's report reveals that Bergotte in fact found him remarkably intelligent, reversing the feared judgment.

appraisal_events.evidence: Swann qui avait pris dans le milieu Guermantes l'habitude de recevoir les grands artistes comme de bons amis à qui on cherche seulement à faire manger les plats qu'ils aiment, jouer aux jeux ou... se livrer aux sports qui leur plaisent.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's ironic aside frames Swann's flattering remark to Bergotte as a routinized, faintly patronizing social habit picked up in the Guermantes milieu, quietly undercutting the sincerity of his hospitality toward artists.

status_effects.explanation: Bergotte's reported esteem for the narrator's intelligence reverses his fear of having appeared foolish, locally elevating him in the eyes of the writer he most admires.
The narrator's private anxiety about having disappointed Bergotte gives way to relief and validation upon learning of his praise.
The narrator's ironic framing exposes Swann's courtesy toward artists as a somewhat mechanical social performance rather than genuine engagement, mildly lowering him.

ambiguities: Bergotte's praise of the narrator reaches the reader only through Gilberte's secondhand, joyfully colored report rather than directly, so its exact force and reliability are not independently confirmed within the passage.
